faqs.question: When is Propose Day 2027, and what day of the week is it?
faqs.answer: Propose Day 2027 is Monday 8 February, the second day of Valentine week. Rose Day is Sunday 7 February and Valentine's Day is Sunday 14 February, so Propose Day falls on a working day.

faqs.question: Should I use aap or tum in a Propose Day message to my wife?
faqs.answer: Use whichever one you already use with her at home. A तुम line in a marriage that runs on आप reads as though it was written for somebody else, and the mismatch is the first thing a Hindi reader notices.

faqs.question: Is it strange to propose to your own wife?
faqs.answer: No. The line is not asking a question that is still open; it is restating a choice. Palit's study of married Indian couples found the partner's response is what makes a disclosure count, so keep it easy to answer.

faqs.question: What is the suniye or ji register?
faqs.answer: It is Hindi with the second-person pronoun dropped entirely, where the verb ending carries the respect instead. In the Hindi Dependency Treebank, 44% of sentences with a second-person verb never name the person at all.

faqs.question: Can my wife send these lines to me instead?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the gender endings flipped. रहा हूँ becomes रही हूँ, चलेंगी becomes चलेंगे, चलोगी becomes चलोगे, and हो जाती हो becomes हो जाते हो.

faqs.question: Can a Hindi line work if we normally speak English at home?
faqs.answer: Sometimes it lands as affectionate and sometimes as performance. If Hindi is nobody's first language in the house, send the line in the language you actually argue in.

faqs.question: How are propose day quotes for a wife different from propose day wishes?
faqs.answer: A quote is a line you copy and adapt for one person. A wish is addressed and sent, often to a friend or relative you are not proposing to at all.

faqs.question: Should I write the line in Devanagari or in Roman Hindi?
faqs.answer: Devanagari if she reads it comfortably, Roman if her phone keyboard or reading habit is English. Every line here carries both, so you can paste either.

faqs.question: Is tu ever right between a husband and wife?
faqs.answer: Only where तू is already the pronoun between you, which is true in parts of north-western India and wrong almost everywhere else. No तू lines are published here for that reason.

faqs.question: Does a forwarded Hindi quote still count?
faqs.answer: Less than a line you changed one word of. The lines here are written to be adapted — swap in a name, a room, a habit she will recognise.

faqs.question: Which SubhSandesh template suits a married couple on Propose Day?
faqs.answer: The proposal scrapbook is built for asking, but for a long-married reader the "I love you" page is usually the better shape. Both are English-language templates; Devanagari text pastes in and displays, but the interface around it stays English.

faqs.question: Can I keep the page private if we share a phone or laptop?
faqs.answer: Yes, a page can be password-protected before it is shared. Platform-wide, 38.7% of creators do exactly that — 1,961 of 5,061 pages across 20 page types, measured 23 September 2026.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Day Quotes for Wife in Hindi: Aap, Tum or Neither

Propose Day quotes for a wife in Hindi fail on the pronoun more often than on the sentiment. Hindi makes you pick आप, तुम or तू before you can say anything affectionate, and many Indian husbands and wives have never used तुम with each other. The 10 lines below are grouped by the register a marriage already runs on, not by how long it has lasted — each in Devanagari, with transliteration and gloss.

Propose Day 2027 is **Monday 8 February**, a working day; Rose Day falls on Sunday 7 and Valentine's Day on Sunday 14. The delivery table later uses SubhSandesh's platform-wide figures: 5,061 pages built since 12 March 2026 across 20 page types, 38.7% of them password-protected before sharing.

## What decides whether a Propose Day line works inside a marriage

Register, not sentiment. Hindi has three second-person pronouns, and a syntax paper on [copular agreement in Hindi-Urdu by Bhatia and Bhatt (Glossa, 2023)](https://www.glossa-journal.org/article/id/5777/) glosses them precisely: तू as 2NH, non-honorific singular; तुम as the neutral second person, taking plural agreement; आप as 2H, honorific, also plural.

A तुम line sent into a marriage where आप is the habit reads as someone else's marriage.

There is a fourth option English lacks. Hindi drops the pronoun and lets the verb ending carry the register alone.

In the 351,704-token Universal Dependencies release of the [Hindi Dependency Treebank built at IIIT Hyderabad](https://ltrc.iiit.ac.in/treebank_H2014/), 163 of 16,649 sentences carry a verb marked Person=2, and only 92 of those — 56% — name the person. In the other 71, about 44%, the verb ending is the only clue.

That is the सुनिए / जी register: no pronoun spoken, the honorific carried by the -इए ending alone. A great many Indian couples talk this way every day.

## Why years married is the wrong way to sort these lines

Most quote pages for wives sort by anniversary count. Indian data suggests that axis carries little.

A cross-sectional study of 199 married healthcare professionals in Gujarat, published in the [Journal of Clinical and Diagnostic Research in December 2024](https://www.jcdr.net/articles/PDF/20379/74909_CE%5BRa1%5D_F(IS)_QC(PS_SS)_PF1(AG_OM)_PFA(IS)_PN(IS).pdf), found duration of marriage had a non-significant correlation with marital quality — r=0.033, p=0.644, in a sample averaging 13.40±10.44 years married. The authors conclude interventions should target communication style, conflict resolution, spousal support and empathy, not demographics.

Eleven years married tells you little. What the couple says to each other tells you a lot.

Manjushree Palit's 2014 Virginia Tech dissertation, [Uncovering Messages of Intimacy in Married Indian Couples](https://vtechworks.lib.vt.edu/items/83f9efe8-0559-430a-bc5b-7298385834a8), interviewed 11 couples (N=22) using pictures as metaphors and found intimacy running across six dimensions. Wives rated emotional closeness and self-disclosure the most important; husbands rated commitment. Her participants kept returning to one sub-theme: the partner's response is crucial, and a disclosure only counts if something comes back.

A Propose Day line after a decade is not a declaration. It is an opening move, and it must be easy to answer.

## 10 Propose Day lines for your wife in Hindi, grouped by register

Pick the group your marriage already speaks in. Endings are written for a husband addressing a wife; each group gives the flip.

### 1. आप register — for marriages where आप never changed

**Who this suits:** couples who used आप at the wedding and never switched — common in north India and joint-family households.
**What the grammar does:** आप takes plural agreement, so the respect sits in the verb: हैं, चलेंगी, आपने.
**The lines:**

> घर आप से है, मकान तो पहले भी था।
> *Ghar āp se hai, makān to pahle bhī thā.*
> "The home is because of you. The house was already here."

> पूछना तो तब ही चाहिए था। आज पूछ रहा हूँ — साथ चलेंगी?
> *Pūchhnā to tab hī chāhiye thā. Āj pūchh rahā hūn — sāth chalengī?*
> "I should have asked back then. I am asking today — will you come with me?"

> आपने जो निभाया है, वो किसी वादे से बड़ा है।
> *Āpne jo nibhāyā hai, vo kisī vāde se baṛā hai.*
> "What you have carried through is bigger than any promise."

**When not to use it:** if you say तुम at home, आप sounds like you are addressing a guest. As a wife: रहा हूँ → रही हूँ, चलेंगी → चलेंगे.

### 2. तुम register — for marriages that switched, or started there

**Who this suits:** couples who moved to तुम at some point, or were friends first. Bhatia and Bhatt's neutral second person — warm without being familiar.
**What the grammar does:** तुम takes 2pl agreement — हो, चलोगी, तुमने — a grade below आप, well above तू.
**The lines:**

> तुमने मेरी सबसे मामूली आदतें भी देख ली हैं, और फिर भी साथ हो।
> *Tumne merī sabse māmūlī ādaten bhī dekh lī hain, aur phir bhī sāth ho.*
> "You have seen even my most ordinary habits, and you are still here."

> तुम चुप हो जाती हो, तो घर में सब कुछ रुक जाता है।
> *Tum chup ho jātī ho, to ghar men sab kuchh ruk jātā hai.*
> "When you go quiet, everything in the house stops."

> शादी के बाद पूछना बंद नहीं करना चाहिए। तो पूछ रहा हूँ — साथ चलोगी?
> *Shādī ke bād pūchhnā band nahīn karnā chāhiye. To pūchh rahā hūn — sāth chalogī?*
> "One should not stop asking after the wedding. So I am asking — will you come with me?"

**When not to use it:** where spouses use आप in front of elders, a तुम line read aloud lands badly. As a wife: हो जाती हो → हो जाते हो, चलोगी → चलोगे.

### 3. No pronoun at all — the सुनिए / जी register

**Who this suits:** the group every English quote list misses — couples who have gone years without a second-person pronoun between them, opening with सुनिए or जी.
**What the grammar does:** the pronoun is dropped and the verb ending carries the register — the 44% pattern above. Lines with no second-person verb are register-neutral, working unedited either way.
**The lines:**

> इतने साल एक ही घर में, और अब भी दरवाज़े की आहट पहचान लेता हूँ।
> *Itne sāl ek hī ghar men, aur ab bhī darvāze kī āhaṭ pahchān letā hūn.*
> "So many years in the same house, and I still know your step at the door."

> सुनिए — कुछ नहीं, बस आवाज़ सुननी थी।
> *Suniye — kuchh nahīn, bas āvāz sunnī thī.*
> "Listen — it is nothing, I just wanted to hear your voice."

> साथ रहना मुश्किल नहीं था। इतने साल बाद भी साथ अच्छा लगना — वो बड़ी बात है।
> *Sāth rahnā mushkil nahīn thā. Itne sāl bād bhī sāth achchhā lagnā — vo baṛī bāt hai.*
> "Staying together was never the hard part. Still liking it after all these years is."

> जी, एक बात कहनी है। और रोज़ कहनी चाहिए थी।
> *Jī, ek bāt kahnī hai. Aur roz kahnī chāhiye thī.*
> "There is something I have to say. And I should have been saying it every day."

**When not to use it:** these are quiet. For an unmistakable ask, use an आप or तुम line. As a wife: पहचान लेता हूँ → पहचान लेती हूँ; the rest need no change.

## Four ways to deliver the line on a working Monday

8 February 2027 is a Monday, so most of these are read between a commute and a meeting. The last column carries SubhSandesh's platform-wide numbers, measured 23 September 2026.

| Delivery | Setup time | Privacy control | Platform-wide evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp message | Under a minute | None; sits in chat backup | 48.4% of shared-page views are on a phone (27,185 of 56,152) |
| Handwritten note | 10–20 minutes | Total, offline | Not measurable here |
| A built page carrying the line | Median 2.4 hours first save to last edit, sampled on /apology-dashboard, n=1,348 | Password used by 38.7% of creators (1,961 of 5,061) | 91.2% of started pages are published (4,615 of 5,061) |

The page is the slow option and the only one with a lock on it. Saying it out loud at the door beats all three. If your household shares a laptop, the lock is the argument.

Once the words are settled, the [proposal scrapbook page](/proposal) is the format built for asking. For a long-married reader that shape is often wrong, and the honest alternative is the ["I love you" page](/love-gf), the #2 page type platform-wide at 1,173 created, 23.2% of all pages.

Both are **English-language templates**: a Devanagari line pasted into a text field displays correctly, but every label and button around it stays in English. If this Propose Day follows a bad patch, the [apology dashboard](/apology-dashboard) is the more honest page — the platform's #1 creation at 1,347 pages, 26.6% across 20 page types.

## What we could not verify, and what we cut

Eighteen lines were drafted, ten published. Every content word was checked against a headword in R. S. McGregor's *Oxford Hindi-English Dictionary* and every inflected form against the Hindi Dependency Treebank: 111 of the 120 word forms in the published lines appear there exactly, 92.5%. The eight that do not are second-person and infinitive forms a newswire corpus barely contains, each confirmed against a published conjugation paradigm.

Eight were cut. Two used आदत for a person, a trope heavy in film lyrics and forwards.

One leaned on त्योहार as a metaphor for ordinary days, generic enough to collide with circulating messages. One was a calque of "I choose you again" — English sentiment in Hindi clothing.

One used the standalone infinitive prohibitive हँसना मत, common in speech but present in the treebank only as another verb's complement. Three were greeting-card lines or repeated an image another line carried.

None of these lines has been reviewed by a native Hindi speaker.

## When a Hindi line is the wrong thing to send

If Hindi is the household's second language, a Devanagari line reads as performance. Send it in her first language instead.

If the marriage is genuinely in trouble, a Propose Day line is the wrong instrument, and no template here fixes that.

And if she is in the next room, say it out loud. Palit's participants were clear that the partner's response makes a disclosure count, and a message cannot give you a face.

structuralLimitations: The Hindi lines were NOT reviewed by a native Hindi speaker. Verification was mechanical: every content word checked against a headword in R. S. McGregor's Oxford Hindi-English Dictionary (dsal.uchicago.edu, fetched but deliberately not cited because that domain hit the 3-post batch cap mid-run), every inflected form checked against the Universal Dependencies release of the Hindi Dependency Treebank (HDTB), and the eight forms HDTB does not attest checked against published conjugation paradigms on en.wiktionary.org. Idiomatic naturalness cannot be established this way.

The HDTB treebank is newswire. It contains no तू and effectively no तुम (तुम = 0 occurrences, तुम्हारे = 1, तुमने = 2), so the तुम paradigm could not be corpus-verified and rests on the dictionary and conjugation-table checks alone. The 44% pronoun-drop figure is therefore measured on a written news register, not on spoken marital Hindi, and should not be read as a rate for conversation.

No SERP was measured for this keyword. Phase 1 was skipped inside the 5-search budget, so this post makes no claim about what competing pages contain, and any inherited competitive framing would be stale. auditReport.honestAssessment: This is a copy-text query with near-zero conversion — the searcher copies a line and leaves — so the page is a visibility asset judged on impressions, not a converting page, and it should not be expected to drive page builds. These SERPs are an annual February news cycle owned by MensXP, Zee, Webdunia and Amar Ujala, whose domain authority is far above ours, so the realistic target is position 6–10, not 3. What an answer engine might cite it for is the one thing no incumbent quote list carries: an original count from a named 351,704-token treebank showing 44% of second-person Hindi sentences drop the pronoun, a published cut-ledger saying which lines were dropped and why, and Indian marriage research showing years married predicts marital quality at r=0.033 — which is the explicit argument against the way every rival page is organised. Against that: no SERP was measured, the Hindi has had no native-speaker review, and ranking takes months regardless.
